intended_object: The induced map G/f⁻¹(H) → P/H on finite quotients, for a continuous homomorphism f : G → P into a pro-p group and an open normal subgroup H of P. It is packaged as a FiniteGrp morphism so it can serve as a component of the cone used to build `lift`. Inferred from the docstring and from its only use, in `lift`.
explanation: This is a helper for the proof, not a notion in its own right. It wraps `QuotientGroup.map` as a morphism between objects of `FiniteGrp`. The source object is the quotient of G by the kernel `preimage p f H`, which the library bundles as a `Quotient p G`. That bundling records that the quotient is a finite p-group, so this kernel is an index in the diagram defining the maximal pro-p quotient. The map is used only to give the components of the cone in `lift` (the universal property of the maximal pro-p quotient). The construction itself is correct: since preimage p f H is H.comap f, the condition `fun _ h ↦ h` holds by definition, and the map sends gK to f(g)H, as it should. Still, it is internal glue for the limit construction, not a standalone mathematical definition to compare with the literature.
